title: NIKE's High P/E Valuation: Can Fundamentals Justify the Premium?
author: Na
description: NIKE's stock has declined 22.9% in three months despite trading at a premium 20.12X forward P/E ratio, exceeding industry average of 17.3X. The company faces persistent weakness in Sportswear, Jordan Brand, and Greater China, with fiscal 2027 revenues expected to decline in the high single digits and EBIT falling faster. Management expects most restructuring benefits to arrive in fiscal 2029-2030, creating a prolonged 'pain before gain' scenario. Analysts recommend avoiding the stock until revenue stabilization and margin recovery emerge.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: NIKE trades at a premium 20.12X forward P/E despite 22.9% stock decline in three months. First-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues declined 4-5%, with persistent weakness in Sportswear (low double-digit decline), Jordan Brand (mid-teens decline), and Greater China (26% decline). Fiscal 2027 revenues expected to decline in high single digits with EBIT falling faster. Earnings estimates revised downward 3% and 2.3% for fiscal 2027 and 2028 respectively. Restructuring benefits delayed until fiscal 2029-2030. Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating.

adidas is mentioned as a peer competitor trading at a lower forward P/E of 12.57X compared to NIKE's 20.12X, suggesting more reasonable valuation. However, adidas shares declined 24.9% in the past three months, slightly underperforming NIKE, indicating sector-wide weakness in athletic apparel.

Steven Madden is cited as a peer with a forward P/E of 17.84X, lower than NIKE's 20.12X. The company outperformed NIKE with 14.6% growth in the past three months, suggesting relative strength but no specific operational details provided.

Wolverine World Wide trades at a lower forward P/E of 10.52X compared to NIKE's 20.12X. The company significantly outperformed NIKE with 10.4% growth in the past three months, indicating relative strength in the sector.

title: Nike Stock Near 52-Week Lows: Can Its Dividend and Caitlin Clark Spark a Rebound?
author: Zacks.Com
description: Nike's Q1 results showed mixed performance with revenue declining 4% year-over-year and weak guidance for fiscal 2027, pushing stock near 52-week lows. While the company's 5% dividend yield is attractive and Caitlin Clark's signature shoe launch shows promise for women's sports growth, significant risks remain including declining sales, Greater China challenges, and weak direct-to-consumer performance. Zacks rates NKE as a Strong Sell.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock down nearly 50% in 2026 and near 52-week lows. Q1 revenue missed consensus estimates with 4% YoY decline, Greater China revenue plunged 26%, digital sales fell 13%, and FY27 guidance projects 14-27% EPS decline. Multiple business segments under pressure despite margin expansion. Zacks rates it Strong Sell.
Mentioned as a fast-growing rival that recently signed global soccer superstar Kylian Mbappé, demonstrating competitive strength in athlete partnerships and market share gains against Nike.

title: NIKE's Cost Controls vs. Growth Investments: Right Tradeoff?
author: Na
description: NIKE announced its Pace program targeting $2.5 billion in cumulative savings through fiscal 2031 by streamlining operations and modernizing supply chains. While reducing less productive spending, the company is increasing demand-creation investments by 5%. However, NIKE expects fiscal 2027 revenues to decline in high single digits due to deliberate portfolio adjustments in Sportswear, Jordan Brand, and Greater China markets.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Expected high single-digit revenue decline in fiscal 2027, stock down 21.6% in past six months, Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and downward EPS estimate revisions in past 30 days outweigh positive aspects of the cost-cutting Pace program.
